chunks: And that which was narrated is: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqi from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid al-Attar from Abu Sa'id al-Mukari who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man killed a lion in the Haram (sanctuary). He said: 'Upon him is a sheep which he must slaughter.'

It is to be understood that he killed it even if he did not intend it, and whenever the matter is upon that, the expiation becomes obligatory upon him. And there is no harm in killing the louse, the flea, and the ant in the Haram if the person is Muhrim (in Ihram), and it is not permissible for him if he is Muhtalim (not in Ihram)? And we have clarified that if he is Muhrim, the expiation becomes obligatory upon him. Narrated.

key_terms.مُحِلًّا: One who is not in the state of Ihram
key_terms.مُحْرِمًا: One who is in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing a lion in the Haram while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between intentional and unintentional killing of game within the Haram, establishing that even accidental slaying of a lion necessitates the expiation of a sheep. It further refines the scope of prohibited creatures by permitting the killing of small insects like lice, fleas, and ants regardless of the pilgrim's state, while noting that the obligation of expiation for these smaller creatures applies specifically when the pilgrim is in the state of Ihram.
